mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds Rate above 5.25% in a given month coincides with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to higher discount rates eroding expected equity payoffs.
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window, 20-day forward returns remain non-negative during high-rate periods, or the FEDFUNDS spike is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) against a control period.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in UNRATE above 4.5% for two consecutive months is associated with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as higher labor-market disengagement reduces consumer wealth and corporate hiring intentions.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses above 4.5% and remains above for ≥2 months
failure_condition: In regimes with low inflation, UNRATE increases without a significant negative 20-day forward return (p > 0.05), or the effect is explained by other variables.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly surge in HOUST (household spending index) exceeding 2% year-over-year coincides with a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as strong consumer demand boosts corporate earnings expectations.
failure_condition: During late-cycle or recessionary periods, HOUST YoY growth > 2% is not associated with positive 20-day forward returns (Rank IC < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in INDPRO (industrial production index) of at least 3% predicts a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return as weak manufacturing momentum raises recession risk and compresses equity valuations.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO declines ≥3% in two consecutive months
failure_condition: During periods of strong demand, INDPRO declines of ≥3% do not produce statistically significant negative 60-day forward returns (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both rise simultaneously by more than 0.25% in a month, the S&P 500 exhibits a positive 20-day forward return as dual price-inflation pressures reduce real rate expectations.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS ↑ > 0.25% AND CPIAUCSL ↑ > 0.25% in the same month
failure_condition: In single-variable tightening episodes, the interaction signal does not produce a statistically significant positive 20-day return (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in PAYEMS (employment months) below 150,000 in a month coincides with a negative 5-day S&P 500 forward return as labor market weakness precedes short-term equity sell-off.
failure_condition: During periods of robust hiring, PAYEMS < 150,000 does not reliably precede negative 5-day returns (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in GDPC1 (real personal consumption) of at least 1% for three consecutive months predicts a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return as persistent demand weakness depresses corporate earnings growth.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 monthly decline ≥1% for ≥3 consecutive months
failure_condition: In periods of strong external demand, GDPC1 declines of ≥1% over 3 months fail to predict negative 60-day forward returns (Rank IC > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: When RSAFS (retail sales) falls by more than 5% in a month relative to the prior month, the S&P 500 shows a negative 20-day forward return as weak retail activity signals consumer pessimism and lower corporate profit expectations.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS monthly decline > 5% vs prior month
failure_condition: During periods of robust retail activity, RSAFS declines > 5% do not precede negative 20-day forward returns (p > 0.05).
